channel.title: The Grant Desk - Journalism & Writers, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Journalism & Writers, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Grant: Ocean Culture Life: Storytelling Grants 2027 (GBP 1,000, 3,000 or 5,000 for ocean stories in any medium) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Ocean Culture Life
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Grants of GBP 1,000, GBP 3,000 and GBP 5,000; applicants choose the level that matches their production costs

Annual grants, now in their fourth year, for creators telling ocean stories in any medium: film, photography, writing, audio, illustration and art.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: The Stringer Awards 2027: multi-year unrestricted cash awards for journalists and creative practitioners exposing abuses of power (aiming for USD 9,000-100,000) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
The Stringer Foundation
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026
Award: Multi-year, unrestricted cash awards; the foundation aims for grants between USD 9,000 and USD 100,000, depending on funds raised. No application fee mentioned.

The Stringer Foundation gives multi-year, unrestricted cash awards to people who use public media to expose abuses of power and injustices that harm the public, while upholding the truth.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: IAS CEU: Global Invisible University Artist and Writer in Residence Fellowships 2027/28 (Budapest, EUR 2,000 a month) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Institute for Advanced Study, Central European University (IAS CEU)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: Net allowance of EUR 2,000 a month, plus accommodation at the Raoul Wallenberg Guesthouse and/or office space at IAS CEU as available. Travel and health insurance are not covered.

Two residential fellowships within the Global Invisible University programme: one Writer in Residence (poetry, prose, drama, screen and playwriting) and one Visual or New Media Artist in Residence (from painting and film to digital art, computer graphics and interactive art).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence 2027-28 (NYPL, Harlem; USD 35,000 long-term or USD 3,000 a month short-term; playwrights and creative writers eligible) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, The New York Public Library
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Long-term fellowship: USD 35,000 stipend. Short-term fellowship: USD 3,000 per month for one to three months. No application fee mentioned.

Residential fellowships for work on the history, politics, literature and culture of peoples of African descent that needs the Schomburg Center's collections.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027, "Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet" (funded six-week residency for researchers, creatives and practitioners) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Monthly allowance for the six-week residency (figure not published: researchers get standard Humboldt fellowship rates, creatives and practitioners a competitive honorarium), travel allowance to and from Germany, accommodation at Schloss Wiepersdorf and a Berlin aparthotel, and a budget for public formats. No family allowance. No application fee.

Each year the Humboldt Foundation brings twelve people from research, the arts and civil society together to work on one topic and find new ways of communicating it to audiences beyond academia. The 2027 topic is Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: McKnight National Residency and Commission 2027-28 (Playwrights' Center; USD 15,000 commission plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds) (closes 14 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Playwrights' Center, funded by the McKnight Foundation
Deadline: 14 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: USD 15,000 commission, plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds to develop the play, including travel and housing. No application fee mentioned.

A commission for one nationally recognised playwright from outside Minnesota to write a new play, developed through workshops at the Playwrights' Center and ending in a public reading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Los Angeles Reporting Collective: LARC 2027 Fellowship (Southern California, USD 600 stipend) (closes 23 Nov)
item.description:
Los Angeles Reporting Collective (LARC)
Deadline: 23 Nov 2026
Award: USD 600 project stipend, paid on completing the training phase, with possible extra funding for project expenses

Yearlong journalism training and mentorship programme for local reporters and nonfiction storytellers. Fellows get 12 free workshops (8 online, 4 in person in Los Angeles), a one-on-one mentor, newsroom shadowing and free conference access, then produce their own project with a USD 600 stipend.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: MPI Short Film Lab 2027: narrative short film lab with fellowship grants and a USD 10,000 script grant (theme: For the Greater Good?) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
Moving Picture Institute (MPI)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026, 23:59 PST
Award: Filmmakers accepted into the lab receive fellowship grants (amount not published). One official selection receives a USD 10,000 grant, which includes MPI acquiring the script for further development. Travel support for the Los Angeles summit is not mentioned. No application fee mentioned.

The Moving Picture Institute is a production company and talent incubator that makes films about human freedom. Its Short Film Lab takes writer-directors from a concept to a finished short script, and can lead to production as an MPI Original film. THEME 2027: For the Greater Good?

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Gordon N. Fisher / JHR Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (Massey College, Toronto; for a journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Massey College, University of Toronto, with Journalists for Human Rights (JHR)
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: CAD 4,900 per month for the eight-month university year, all University of Toronto fees, and round-trip economy airfare to and from Toronto. No application fee mentioned.

One place alongside the William Southam Journalism Fellows at Massey College, University of Toronto, reserved for a journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East. The fellow spends the academic year in Toronto auditing university courses and taking part in college life.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: LCC-CBA Journalism Fellowship 2027 (CAD 40,000 for four long-form articles on law and justice in Canada) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
Law Commission of Canada and Canadian Bar Association
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026
Award: CAD 40,000 stipend, paid quarterly on submission of each completed article. No application fee mentioned.

A one-year fellowship for a journalist to report in depth on how the law affects people's lives in Canada, now in its third year. WHO: journalists based in Canada with at least five years of full-time work experience who want to deepen their knowledge of the justice system.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: William Southam Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (Massey College, University of Toronto; CAD 4,900 a month for eight months) (closes 1 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Massey College, University of Toronto
Deadline: 1 Feb 2027
Award: CAD 4,900 per month for the eight-month university year (CAD 39,200), all university fees, and book expenses of up to CAD 600. No application fee mentioned.

Up to three mid-career journalists spend an academic year at Massey College, a graduate college within the University of Toronto, auditing courses of their choice and taking part in college life.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Fonds BJP Press Play 2027: Development Programme for Journalistic Makers (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Fonds BJP (Fonds voor Bijzondere Journalistieke Projecten)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: EUR 3,200 towards about 20 days of time invested, plus a personal coach and workshops. No application fee.

Press Play helps makers develop and pitch a journalistic or creative project, with five places in each of four tracks: audio, video, writing and photo.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: The Aftermath Project: 2026 Post-Conflict Photography Grant (USD 25,000) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
The Aftermath Project
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: One USD 25,000 production grant (paid 50% at start, 40% midway, 10% on delivery); four additional finalists named. No application fee stated.

The Aftermath Project funds documentary photographers telling the other half of the story of conflict: what it takes for individuals, communities and nations to rebuild and heal after war.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Sundance Episodic Lab 2027: Alfred P. Sloan Grant Track (science and technology series) (closes 3 Dec)
item.description:
Sundance Institute with the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
Deadline: 3 Dec 2026
Award: USD 17,000 grant plus creative support through the Episodic Lab. Submission fee waived with code EpSloanGrantX121426 on FilmFreeway.

An extended Sloan-only round of the Sundance Episodic Lab for original half-hour or one-hour series whose subject is science, technology or mathematics, or a scientist, engineer or mathematician. Open to a writer or a two-person writing team.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: IWMF: Fund for Indigenous Journalists and Allies (Reporting on MMIP/MMIWG2T) (rolling)
item.description:
International Women's Media Foundation (IWMF)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Grants average up to USD 5,000; proposals over USD 10,000 considered on a limited basis. Plus editorial and pitching support. No application fee stated.

The IWMF Fund for Indigenous Journalists supports in-depth reporting on Missing and Murdered Indigenous People, Women, Girls and Two-Spirit people (MMIP/MMIWG2T).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Kent Cultural Alliance SFW Residency, Spring 2027 "SERVICE": six-week live-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland (USD 7,500 stipend) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kent Cultural Alliance
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: USD 7,500 stipend for the six-week session, travel reimbursed up to USD 1,000, studio and gallery expenses reimbursed up to USD 1,500, and on-site housing with a private en-suite bedroom. No application fee.

A community-engaged residency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Three artists live and work for six weeks in the Raimond Cultural Center, a restored historic house, around the theme SERVICE, working with local partners For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: City of Kitchener 2027 Artist in Residence (CAD 10,000 honorarium) (closes 3 Dec)
item.description:
City of Kitchener
Deadline: 3 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: CAD 10,000 honorarium (two instalments) plus up to CAD 2,500 for pre-approved expenses. No application fee.

The City of Kitchener's 2027 Artist in Residence is a six-month, part-time residency for a contemporary artist working at the boundaries of writing, academic or archival research and visual arts.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: EFA SHIFT x Momus Residency 2027: six-month programme for New York artists who write and writers who make art (USD 2,000 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts (EFA Studios) with Momus
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Artist honorarium of USD 2,000, within a six-month residency at EFA Studios with monthly critical seminars and mentoring. No application fee stated.

A new iteration of EFA's SHIFT Residency, run with the art criticism platform Momus and focused on where artistic practice meets critical writing.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Saari Residence 2028 (Kone Foundation, Finland; monthly grant plus housing and workspace) (closes 31 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kone Foundation, Saari Residence
Deadline: 31 Mar 2027, 16:00 EEST
Award: Monthly grant for living, travel and other costs, plus accommodation and workspace. The 2028 figure is not yet published; the 2027 cycle paid EUR 2,700, 3,200 or 3,800 per month depending on career stage. No application fee.

Saari Residence is the Kone Foundation's residency in rural southwest Finland, applied for a year in advance. Residents get housing, a workspace and a monthly grant (EUR 2,700 to 3,800 per month in the 2027 cycle, depending on career stage; 2028 figures not yet published).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Schloss Wiepersdorf Individual and Collaborative Fellowships 2028 (Brandenburg; EUR 1,200/month plus room and board) (closes 15 Apr 2027)
item.description:
Schloss Wiepersdorf (state of Brandenburg)
Deadline: 15 Apr 2027, 23:59 CEST
Award: EUR 1,200 per month stipend, a one-time EUR 480 material grant, room and board, and German visa costs where needed. No application fee.

Three-month residential fellowships at Schloss Wiepersdorf for artists, writers, composers and scholars from Germany and abroad. Fellows get room, board, a EUR 1,200 monthly stipend and a material grant; fine artists get a studio where space allows.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Yale Law School Information Society Project: Resident Fellowship 2027-2028 (closes 10 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Yale Law School, Information Society Project (ISP)
Deadline: 10 Jan 2027
Award: USD 70,000 per year plus Yale benefits and a travel stipend. No application fee.

Postdoctoral resident fellowships at Yale ISP for scholars of law and technology, with AI as a stated priority alongside the digital public sphere, content moderation, privacy, antitrust and algorithmic governance.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Folger Institute Artistic Research Fellowships 2027-28 (USD 4,000 to 5,000 per month) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Folger Shakespeare Library (Folger Institute)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 4,000 per virtual month or USD 5,000 per onsite month.

Artistic research fellowships for artists whose work needs primary research on the early modern world (about 1400 to 1800) and its legacies, using the Folger's collections. ELIGIBILITY: any artist; no degree required and no citizenship rule stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (Columbia Journalism School) (closes 4 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Spencer Fellowship at Columbia Journalism School
Deadline: 4 Feb 2027
Award: Residential stipend USD 85,000 or non-residential stipend USD 43,000, plus a USD 7,500 travel and research budget. Non-residential fellows also get airfare and hotel for required NYC trips. No application fee.

The Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship, based at Columbia Journalism School, supports ambitious, research-savvy storytellers producing books, magazine features, documentaries and podcasts that deepen public understanding of critical issues in education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BFI NETWORK England: Early Development Fund (GBP 3,000-5,000 treatment awards for debut long-form writers) (closes 11 Nov)
item.description:
BFI NETWORK (BFI, National Lottery funding)
Deadline: 11 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,000 to 5,000 per project to develop a treatment (stage one). Projects completed to schedule can then apply for second-stage funding to write a full first draft. National Lottery funding; no application fee stated.

BFI NETWORK's Early Development Fund supports writers at the very start of a debut long-form project: those who do not yet have a first draft of a script (or the equivalent format for immersive work).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (University of Michigan) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 85,000 stipend plus USD 5,000 relocation (figures from secondary listings; confirm on the official site).

An academic-year fellowship for mid-career journalists to pursue a study project at the University of Michigan, with seminars and programming at Wallace House. DEADLINES: international applicants 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm ET; US applicants 1 February 2027. No application fee stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: National Geographic Society: The Human Thread RFP (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
National Geographic Society (Center for Human Histories and Cultures, with support from Lilly Endowment Inc.)
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Level I: up to US$20,000 (for applicants new to National Geographic funding, one year to implement). Level II: up to US$100,000 (for more established applicants, two years to implement).

Request for proposals from the National Geographic Society's Center for Human Histories and Cultures, funded by Lilly Endowment Inc.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cove Park Awarded Residencies 2027-2028 (Scotland, UK, Central and South America and diasporas) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
Cove Park
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Fully funded: GBP 775 per week fee (VAT inclusive, freelance), travel allowance (Scotland GBP 65 to 200, rest of UK up to GBP 250, Europe up to GBP 400, other international up to GBP 1,250), materials up to GBP 150 for studio-based practitioners, private accommodation and studio, visa and access support. Application Access Bursary available (request by 30 November 2026). No application fee.

Cove Park's biennial call for fully funded Awarded Residencies at its 50-acre rural residency site in Argyll, on the west coast of Scotland, programmed between May 2027 and December 2028.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: HKADC Cultural Exchange Project Grant (up to HKD 500,000 for Hong Kong artists working abroad) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Hong Kong Arts Development Council (HKADC)
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026, 18:00 Hong Kong time
Award: General Version: up to HKD 500,000 for individual artists and arts organisations, covering all project expenditure except listed exclusions; up to HKD 800,000 for experienced organisations with large-scale, outstanding exchange projects. Trial Version: up to HKD 150,000 for transportation, freight, insurance and documentation only. No application fee stated.

The Hong Kong Arts Development Council's Cultural Exchange Project Grant supports Hong Kong artists and arts organisations taking work abroad: overseas exhibitions, performances, festival participation, residencies, touring and similar exchange activity, across music, dance, xiqu, drama, visual...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: HKADC Emerging Artists Development Grant (up to HKD 90,000, Hong Kong arts graduates) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
Hong Kong Arts Development Council (HKADC)
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026, 18:00 Hong Kong time
Award: Grant ceiling HKD 90,000 per project (HKADC may exceed the ceiling for projects of great potential, subject to resources). No application fee stated.

The Hong Kong Arts Development Council's Emerging Artists Development Grant funds a first arts project by recent graduates: performances, exhibitions, publications, creation of artwork, translation and other project types allowed under its general Project Grant.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) (closes 9 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
Deadline: 9 Jan 2027
Award: USD 87,500 stipend over 9.5 months, plus USD 5,000 for travel and housing, health insurance and a childcare subsidy. No application fee.

An academic-year fellowship at MIT for journalists covering science, health, technology or the environment, with seminars, MIT and Harvard courses and a self-directed study project.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Freelancer Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border teams of freelance journalists) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: Up to EUR 20,000 per team, plus training and mentoring.

A strand of IJ4EU for freelance journalists: teams of at least two freelancers in two eligible countries receive funding, training and mentoring for a cross-border investigation.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Investigation Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border investigative journalism) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: EUR 5,000 to 50,000 per project, from a EUR 1.2 million pot.

IJ4EU funds cross-border investigative journalism in the public interest, by teams of journalists and newsrooms working across at least two eligible countries. Eligibility is by country of residence, not citizenship; applications are in English.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Outrider AI + Nuclear Reporting Fund (rolling)
item.description:
Outrider Foundation
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 10,000 per reporting project.

Outrider funds journalists and outlets reporting on the intersection of artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons: how AI is changing nuclear risk, command and control, and policy. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Google Form linked from the fund page. No application fee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Inciter Art (Fractured Atlas): quarterly open call for essays, 'tending to the hearth' (USD 750 stipend)
item.description: Fractured Atlas (Inciter Art) · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · USD 750 stipend per selected writer, paid by ACH deposit or check once the first draft is finished (a W-9 form is required). No submission fee.
